#2093. Sabatini vs Gasperini: “Spintonò Massara davanti alla Roma”. Poi il rischio querela e le scuse

Prima le accuse, poi il rischio di una querela e infine le scuse. Walter Sabatini fa marcia indietro dopo aver raccontato un presunto episodio che avrebbe coinvolto Gian Piero Gasperini e Frederic Massara alla Roma. L'ex dirigente giallorosso aveva accusato l'allenatore di aver spintonato il direttore sportivo davanti alla squadra, nel corso della scorsa stagione. Dichiarazioni pesanti, alle quali Gasperini ha scelto di non replicare pubblicamente, pur dando mandato ai propri legali di tutelarlo nelle sedi opportune.

Tutto nasce da un'intervista concessa da Sabatini al Quotidiano Nazionale. Interpellato su Gasperini, l'ex dirigente di Roma e Inter aveva risposto: “Gasperini, bravissimo. Però è diverso da come appare. La scorsa stagione è arrivato a spintonare Massara davanti alla squadra”. Poi un'ulteriore accusa: “Lo ha delegittimato per agevolare i suoi amici. Lo avesse fatto a me, lo avrei preso a pugni...”. Parole che hanno rapidamente fatto il giro dei media, arrivando anche all'attenzione dell'allenatore. Gasperini ha deciso di non commentare la ricostruzione, né nell'immediato né in futuro, mentre dalla Roma è filtrata la notizia del mandato affidato agli avvocati per valutare le iniziative a tutela del tecnico.

La vicenda ha però registrato un nuovo sviluppo con le scuse pubbliche di Sabatini. Attraverso il proprio profilo Instagram, l'ex dirigente ha spiegato il contesto nel quale erano maturate le sue dichiarazioni: “Nel corso di un’intervista dedicata a un libro al quale sono particolarmente affezionato, Lo straniero di Albert Camus, ho fatto riferimento a Gian Piero Gasperini, allenatore della Roma”. Sabatini ha quindi riconosciuto di aver sbagliato: “Non ho alcuna difficoltà ad ammettere di aver sbagliato e a chiedere scusa. Ero molto coinvolto nei temi affrontati dal romanzo, nel tentativo di esplorare le affinità e i comportamenti del protagonista dell’opera, nei quali mi riconosco inesorabilmente. Chiedo sinceramente scusa a Gasperini e a tutti coloro che possano essersi sentiti colpiti dalle mie parole”.

#2092. MN: Why Milan and Inter are calm despite Council request over new stadium plan

A potential obstacle has already arisen after the Generali Stadium announcement, even if all parties remain calm for now.

As MilanNews recall, Tuesday morning’s edition of Corriere della Sera carried a report that had everyone on edge, just days after the renderings of the project were published. However, by the afternoon some quite important clarifications had arrived from Mayor Giuseppe Sala.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The newspaper reported that the Milan City Council had approved a bipartisan measure to halt the current environmental assessment process for the Generali Stadium project and request a new one that encompasses all the interventions the two clubs intend to undertake.

This includes the demolition of the current stadium once the new stadium is operational. The goal is to make the green light for the work conditional on a prior Health Impact Assessment (HIA).

MilanNews have learned that the City Council’s motion is non-binding, meaning Mayor Sala’s administration will not be obligated to follow the council’s request. More importantly, it does not suspend the Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA).

The two clubs remain calm regarding the next phases, especially since the SEA and the VIS are two separate and distinct phases that must both be addressed before work on the new stadium can begin.

The Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is a procedure established by Italian and European legislation that evaluates the environmental sustainability of a plan or program prior to its approval.

It differs from the subsequent Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), which instead examines the environmental effects of a specific project prior to its potential authorisation and implementation.

The Council has therefore advanced a request that would not currently be foreseen under normal formal procedures. In any case, the two clubs are confident in the material produced, providing even more than necessary by integrating the Environmental Report with all the health-related details currently available.

Milan and Inter have no intention of avoiding any type of assessment. On the contrary, the EIA is scheduled for early 2027, by spring, with completion expected within a few months. Further investigations into the project and its impacts will therefore be undertaken shortly, as per the timetable.

Yesterday afternoon, Mayor Sala issues a statement on the news that broke, once again emphasising that the project will move forward.

“It’s clear that continuing to call the stadium issue into question is a gift to the right. I don’t want us to delude ourselves into thinking we’ve already won. I respect the City Council’s opinion, but the Council will respect the fact that I have no intention of reconsidering,” he said.

“We’ll discuss it in the City Council, but I have no intention of reconsidering the stadium. We’ve been talking about it for three years; everyone should do what they think best. I will continue to be consistent, and I will try to move forward with the stadium project.”

Councillor Martina Riva also gave a comment to MilanNews too: “Small obstacles? They won’t be a problem, we are convinced of the validity of our operation and we will move forward: the city, the teams and the fans who want a fully accessible stadium deserve it.

“I really like the Generali Stadium, it has exceeded all expectationsaccessibleI really like the Generali Stadium, it has exceeded all expectations.”

#2091. Stoke City won’t regret selling 27-year-old in the summer transfer window: Opinion

Stoke City cashed in on the attacker on 1st September and he penned a four-year deal at the MKM Stadium running until June 2030. Since leaving SCFC, he has made six appearances for the Tigers in all competitions and has chipped in with one assist.

Thomas, 27, was a key player for the Potters during his time at the Bet365 Stadium and was one of their key players under Mark Robins. He made 52 outings for the Staffordshire outfit in all competitions, scoring 10 goals laying on 15 assists for his ex-teammates.

Robins’ side haven’t missed him at all though and they are sat joint-top of the Championship table along with Birmingham City and Middlesbrough. They are positioned in 3rd on goal difference behind Boro and they are in the play-offs along with Wolves, West Brom, Swansea City, Southampton and QPR after 15 fixtures.

Stoke City won 2-1 away at Portsmouth last time out before the international break after goals by Jack McGlynn and Ben Wilmot. They are back in action next weekend at home to Birmingham City.

Stoke City have flourished since Thomas’ departure. SCFC are less reliant on one player and it has become more of a team effort.

The Wales international, who has 31 caps to his name, hasn’t been able to make the impact he would have wanted to at Hull City. He missed out on their recent squads against Brentford and Ipswich Town and was left on the bench last Saturday against Arsenal.

Thomas faces a tough battle to get into the Tigers’ starting XI in the top flight. They are positioned in 13th in the league and have adapted pretty well to the step up a division against the odds.

Stoke City signed the London-born man back in 2025. Prior to his switch, he had permanent spells at Boreham Wood and Huddersfield Town, as well as loans at Blackburn Rovers and FC Nantes.

Thomas was a great player for Stoke City and his numbers were very impressive. He deserved a big move to Hull City off the back of his form at SCFC.

However, the Potters are better off without him now and have others players stepping up. Robins’ men will be full of confidence at the moment and will be aiming to keep their momentum going against Birmingham City next Saturday.

#2090. Manifesta inferiorità: l'Italia perde di nuovo col Belgio e saluta la Nations League

L'Italia è fuori dalla Nations League 2026/27. La squadra di Roberto Mancini stasera ha perso 4-1 a Bruxelles contro il Belgio e ha chiuso il gruppo A1 al terzo posto, alle spalle dei diavoli rossi e della Francia che ha battuto la Turchia. Nonostante l'iniziale vantaggio azzurro firmato Pio Esposito allo stadio Re Baldovino non c'è stata storia: già prima della mezz'ora i padroni di casa erano avanti 3-1 grazie alle reti di De Cuyper, Ngoy e Doku, poi a dieci dal termine il milanista Moreira ha fissato il punteggio sul definitivo 4-1.

Il migliore dell'Italia nonostante le quattro reti incassate è stato il capitano Donnarumma. "Non eravamo fenomeni dopo la Francia, non siamo scarsi adesso", le parole del numero uno del Manchester City. L'altra sufficienza è stata al centravanti Esposito che ha sbloccato il match dopo undici minuti, ma che nel finale ha anche sbagliato un rigore. I suoi numeri sono comunque importantissimi: 10 reti in 15 gare con la Nazionale, ha già raggiunto grandi attaccanti in termini di realizzazioni come Cassano e Zola. Dall'altro lato, De Bruyne e Doku hanno letteralmente dominato il match: per entrambi 8 in pagella.

Al termine della gara, questa l'analisi di Roberto Mancini: “Penso che abbiamo fatto un po’ di fatica a livello fisico, che abbiamo pagato un po’ la partita con la Francia. Eravamo un po’ in difficoltà fisica. Però sono stati migliori e hanno meritato di vincere, Eravamo partiti bene, volevamo fare quella partita lì. Poi abbiamo preso subito il pareggio e non siamo riusciti a recuperare. Capita che gli altri siano migliori. Rifarebbe le scelte iniziali? Sì, le ho fatte perché volevo vedere due giocatori che non avevo mai visto a certi livelli Koleosho e Pisilli. Sono due giocatori bravi, la sofferenza è stata nella squadra, non nel giocatore".

#2088. Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

McLoughlin 27, A. Gudjohnsen 48Yellow card: Pickering ​34, Cantwell 35, ‌Forshaw 45Attendance: 30,984Referee: Farai ⁠Hallam

“I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a big call.”

“We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”

“It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is important. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”

“Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”

Raul Jimenez reacts after his late penalty saved a point for Wolves against Blackburn 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/aXvVeWw6fc

“Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case.  Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”

“Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”

Bentley spills the corner but gets a free-kick. Moments later, the referee blows his whistle for the final time and the game ends level at 2-2. A dramatic opening night of the new Championship season at Molineux. If the Championship continues in this vein all season, it will be one hell of a year.

Blackburn nearly score a late winner as Garrett’s shot is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a later Blackburn corner.

He sends Toth the wrong way and calmly slots home to bring Wolves level in added time. That penalty decision will certainly create some debate. The Championship is always full of drama and we get some on opening night.

Desperate long balls being sent forward but Blackburn look comfortable for now. The home fans are quite audibly unhappy with this second-half showing.

Wolves do not currently look like scoring an equaliser.

Mosquera is struggling with a knock but Wolves made all five changes. If he is unable to continue, Wolves will have to finish off with ten men.

The frustration inside Molineux is growing and the home fans want to see some more urgency from their side as they trail with under 10 minutes left.

Blackburn are now going to make their final two alterations of the night as Ribeiro and Garrett come on.

Wolves are going to make their final two substitutions as Lima and Chirewa replace Moller Wolfe and Andre.

Blackburn are looking pretty comfortable right now defending their lead and counter-attacking effectively.

Ohashi is penalised for a foul on F Lopez not far outside the Blackburn penalty area and that was pretty harsh on Ohashi. Jimenez is lining this one up as is F Lopez.

Can Wolves turn the game back in their favour? It’s all a bit slow now from the hosts followed by the first signs of disgruntlement from the home supporters.

His father Eidur would have been happy with a striker’s finish like that.

The first half is brought to a close at Molineux and an engaging opening 45 minutes of the new Championship season results in this game being level at 1-1 at the break. Munetsi put Wolves in front before McLoughlin equalised for Blackburn.

Forshaw is the third Blackburn player into the book tonight as the referee goes back to penalise the midfielder for an earlier foul on Andre. That was not Forshaw’s first foul either.

With no VAR or hydration breaks, there will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Mane wins it back for his side on the edge of his own penalty area and drives forward. He takes it across the halfway line before feeding a lovely pass to his right to find Armstrong, whose shot is blocked.

Mane comes close to a stunner. Trippier rolls the ball across the face of the penalty area to 18-year-old Mane, who takes on the shot first time but his effort goes just over the bar.

Wolves come close to restoring their lead. Mane drives inside from the left and plays the ball forward to F Lopez, who takes one touch before getting his shot away from just outside the box. He tries to pick out the top corner but it just misses the target.

Like London buses, two yellow cards come at once and another Blackburn player is into the book. It is their captain Cantwell who receives a yellow card for delaying the restart. Cantwell was not too impressed with that decision.

Both teams off the mark for the season now, a brilliant near-post run and header from McLoughlin who scores his first-ever goal in English football to level the game up.

Molineux briefly stunned into silence. A slight delay from the fans celebrating the header as well.

The first booking of the Championship season goes the way of Blackburn left-back Pickering. It is a pretty simple decision for the referee as Pickering cynically pulls back R Gomes, who had spun him, and rightly receives a yellow card.

R Gomes delivers a cross from the right side of the Blackburn box across the penalty area but Armstrong does not pre-empt that and is not on hand to meet it. However, Alebiosu, with Mane not far behind him, puts it behind for a corner. Trippier delivers and the Blackburn keeper makes a meal of it, missing his punch out but then scrambles back towards his own goal to gather the loose ball.

The visitors went behind against the run of play but probably deservedly they are back on level terms. Morishita clips in the cross from the right to the near post, where McLoughlin meets it first and guides a powerful header into the far corner. Two goals in the opening half an hour of the new Championship season.

"They STUN Molineux!" 😳Sean Mcloughlin delightfully heads past Dan Bentley to equalise for Blackburn 👏 pic.twitter.com/v5qLhJ0wBt

Blackburn are getting great joy down their right through Alebiosu and Morishita, with the latter winning them a corner as Toti is forced to head behind from a cross. Pickering sends it into a good area and the touch comes off the head of Munetsi, whose header loops into the air and goes just over his own bar for another corner on the other side.

Cantwell’s delivery to the far post is headed away.

We have the first goal of the season and it’s the returning Marshall Munetsi who gets it.

A cool finish from the midfielder after a bit of a drab start from the home side.

That will please the new Wolves boss. Such a simple move but the home side ripped Blackburn wide open with two passes.

Work to do for the visitors now who had probably started the better of the two teams before the opener.

Wolves fans make their feelings about VAR known following the goal. No VAR in the Championship of course but no VAR was needed for that anyway. A perfectly good goal.

Mane cuts inside from the left onto his preferred right foot and curls a dangerous ball into the box that is punched away by Toth in the Blackburn goal. 18-year-old Mane was one of very few bright spots for Wolves last season and in many ways it is a surprise that no Premier League teams have lured him back to the top flight quite yet. That could though still happen before the deadline.

The first goal of the Championship season comes against the run of play. It is a clinical, ruthless goal that comes from an incisive pass and clinical finish. The pass is fed through by F Lopez to pick out the run of Munetsi, who is cool, calm and collected as he finishes past Toth. Blackburn had been the better side up until that point but Wolves take the lead at Molineux.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

A shot on target for Blackburn but an easy save in the end. Alebiosu, who has looked good in these early stages, drives down Blackburn’s right before cutting it back to Morishita on the edge of the box. Morishita takes one touch before shooting but his effort is tame and straight at Bentley.

Blackburn have definitely been the better side in these early exchanges, dominating possession and looking a threat going forward.

Blackburn may be heavy underdogs tonight but they have settled down well away at one of the favourites to get promoted. Tony Mowbray may well be seeing this as a good time to play Wolves away.

Alebiosu shows quick feet down Blackburn’s right and clips a cross to the back post, where Afolayan meets it but his header is just off target.

Safe to say the doom and gloom of last season appears to have lifted at Molineux. The home fans in fine voice early on here.

By contrast, Kieran Trippier’s first touch of the season is greeted by loud boos by the travelling Blackburn supporters.

In fact, every Trippier touch is greeted by a chorus of boos. Will they keep that up all game?

They’ve certainly not forgotten his Burnley connection.

New managers and new signings galore. This should be a fascinating spectacle.

He may not be in the starting XI tonight but Jimenez is being serenaded by the home fans on his return to Wolves after a few years away at Fulham. Jimenez and his wife have paid for 5,000 scarves for the Wolves fans tonight.

Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray did say ahead of the game that Wolves have not been used to winning games over the last 12 months so can the visitors take advantage of that tonight? Blackburn are underdogs tonight and not too much is expected of them this season so surely they have nothing to lose this evening?

Due to his Burnley ties, new Wolves defender Trippier is booed by the travelling Blackburn fans. On the other side of defence for Wolves is Moller Wolfe, who started for Norway against England in the World Cup quarter-finals in Miami.

After Jeff Beck’s Hi Ho Silver Lining rings around the stadium and tributes paid to former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes, we are under way at Molineux. The 2026/27 Championship season is officially under way.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off on opening night in the Championship.

Wolves: Bentley; Trippier, Mosquera, T.Gomes; R.Gomes, André, Munetsi, Möller Wolfe; Lopez, Mané; Armstrong.Substitutes: Sá, Bueno, Jiménez, Lima, Doyle, Chirewa, Djiga, Tchatchoua, Edozie.

Blackburn: Toth; Alebiosu, Atcheson, McLoughlin, Pickering; Forshaw, Montgomery; Afolayan, Cantwell, Morishita; Gudjohnsen.Substitutes: Pears, Ribeiro, Tavares, Morsy, Fevrier, Carter, Henriksson, Ohashi, Garrett.

These do not look good if you are a Blackburn fan; these are their attacking statistics and rankings in the Championship last season:

Goals: 42, 23rdxG performance: -13.9, 24thShots on target: 146, 23rdShot conversion: 7.9%, 22ndChances created: 368, 21st

Near the bottom of the league in every single one of those pretty much.

A debut for our brand new away kit 🤩#WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Qxyvw1jAgi

Former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes has died aged 79 in the last week and the club he played 382 times for is paying tribute to him tonight:

Paying tribute to a Wolves legend on tonight's matchday programme 🧡 pic.twitter.com/VEHciTuOZq

"We know what we are doing" 🤝Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto is confident in his side ahead of his the first Championship game of the season 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/2m12gsJ2y8

"We're ready for a strong performance" 💪Wolves defender Kieran Trippier and Blackburn's Sam Morsy preview their opening game of the season clash 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/I5t1J9Gapp

When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager new to English football, it proved a vintage season.

Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

“I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

“There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”

Our experts have been having their say ahead of the new Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:

It is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.

The boys are in the Black Country 👋 #WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/WjuGwrxYtQ

Saturday:Bolton vs PrestonBristol City vs MillwallCharlton vs DerbyMiddlesbrough vs LincolnNorwich vs West BromPortsmouth vs QPRStoke vs SwanseaSheffield United vs Birmingham

Sunday:Watford vs SouthamptonBurnley vs West Ham

🔢 Team news...2⃣ changes✅ Kristi Montgomery & Andri Gudjohnsen come in🆕 Sam Morsy on the bench🤕 Augustus Kargbo, Dion De Neve, Scott Wharton, Moussa Baradji, Mathias Jorgensen & Lewis Miller on the injured list#WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/esyE5Fibqc

☝️ One change from Port Vale🇳🇴 Wolfe in at LB🇪🇸 Hugo misses out with minor groin issueOur line-up for tonight's @EFL Championship opener 📋 pic.twitter.com/oRpIymUw1k

The 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are new playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

Wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

“I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

“It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our big goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”

They have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

Blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

“I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray said. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”

These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

#2086. Wolves should challenge Birmingham City and Middlesbrough for perfect Andre partner: Opinion

Wolves need to be keeping their options open for the January window despite a decent start to the season. Cesar Peixoto’s side currently sit 4th in the Championship and a good window will put them in a very strong position to push for automatic promotion.

Wolves should be keeping a close eye on Arthur Avom ahead of the January transfer window, with the Lorient midfielder offering an opportunity to strengthen their promotion push while potentially laying the foundations for a Premier League midfield.

The 21-year-old has emerged as an attractive target for several English clubs, with Birmingham City and Middlesbrough reportedly tracking his situation. However, Wolves should be looking to get ahead of their Championship rivals, particularly given the opportunity to negotiate a relatively affordable deal.

Avom has already established himself in French football, making 31 Ligue 1 appearances last season after helping Lorient win promotion from the second tier in 2024/25. He has continued to feature regularly this term and has also earned senior international recognition with Cameroon.

His contract situation makes the opportunity even more interesting. Lorient’s agreement with Avom currently runs until June 2027, potentially leaving the French club with limited leverage next summer.

The biggest attraction is how well Avom could complement Andre. Wolves already have an established midfield anchor in the Brazilian, who committed his future to the club until 2030 following relegation from the Premier League.

Andre provides defensive discipline, composure and the ability to dictate possession, whereas Avom offers greater mobility, energy and forward-running ability. The Cameroonian is comfortable winning possession, carrying the ball through midfield and contributing defensively, making him a natural candidate to operate alongside Andre in a double pivot.

That partnership could be particularly valuable across a demanding 46-game Championship campaign, allowing Andre to concentrate on controlling games while Avom supplies the athleticism and intensity needed to compete in both boxes.

There is also a longer-term argument for the move. Much of Wolves’ existing midfield group is already established, with Marshall Munetsi approaching 30 and Tommy Doyle and Boubacar Traore in their mid-twenties.

Avom would introduce another young option alongside Jordan James, helping reduce the need for an extensive midfield rebuild if promotion is secured. His experience in Ligue 1 and international football also means he would not necessarily need several seasons to adapt to a higher level.

Wolves cannot afford to overlook the immediate competition, either. Birmingham and Middlesbrough are both capable of offering attractive projects, while previous Premier League interest demonstrates Avom’s growing reputation.

If Wolves are serious about building a team capable of returning to the top flight and staying there, Avom is exactly the type of recruitment they should be considering. A January move could strengthen their promotion ambitions while giving them a potentially long-term partner for Andre.

#2085. GdS: Milan open to Camarda loan to aid development – move abroad also possible

AC Milan’s plan to strengthen the attack in January could have a knock-on impact on Francesco Camarda’s fate, a report claims.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport makes the bold claim that Milan are readying a winter attempt for Nicolo Tresoldi of Club Brugge. His price tag is already €50m, but the idea is to invest in the young striker and potentially pair him with Goncalo Ramos.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Tresoldi’s fate intersects with that of Camarda. The Milan academy graduate has barely exceeded 100 minutes of playing time this season, 119 to be precise: 83 in the Europa League, with a single start against Salzburg, and another 36 in Serie A.

He hasn’t scored and had only one real chance to score, against Bologna. He needs to play to showcase his qualities, so the club believe it’s best to try do this elsewhere, before returning fit and ready to play for the Rossoneri.

The new development is that Camarda could develop at another Serie A team, or potentially return further enriched by experience abroad. There’s no shortage of options outside of Italy, but it will be a dry loan with no option to make it permanent.

Having arrived as a child in the Milan youth academy, he won an U15 Scudetto. He also achieved a historic record: with a federal exemption required because he was still a teenager, Camarda made his Serie A debut for AC Milan on 25 November 2023, late in the match against Fiorentina.

On that occasion, he became the youngest debutant in Serie A history (15 years, 8 months, and 15 days) and the youngest debutant in Milan’s history, surpassing the previous record set by Paolo Maldini, who made his debut at 16 years, 6 months, and 25 days.

In 2024, he signed his first professional contract and began his experience with Milan Futuro, the club’s second team, created specifically to nurture Milan’s talents, without necessarily having the need to send them elsewhere to develop.

That same season, at 16 years and 226 days, he became the youngest Italian player ever to make his Champions League debut. In 2025-26, it was time to try Serie A, where he could consistently play: he moved to Lecce, where, in 23 appearances, he scored his first (and so far only) league goal.

He was bought by the Giallorossi, and then bought back by Milan (who reserved a buy-back clause), with a contract extended until the summer of 2031 in the summer, plus an option for another year.

After progressing through Italy’s youth teams, Camarda truly found his calling with the U21s, scoring four goals in six games. He was also called up to the senior national team, playing for Baldini’s ‘experimental’ squad, making two appearances.

#2084. Calciomercato no stop - Indiscrezioni, trattative e retroscena del 15 novembre

ROMA, DE ROON VERSO IL RINNOVO. NAPOLI, DE BRUYNE PUÒ PARTIRE A GENNAIO -    Giorni di lavoro intenso per Tony D'Amico, impegnato a programmare il futuro della Roma tra operazioni di mercato e rinnovi contrattuali. La dirigenza giallorossa sta valutando diverse situazioni, con particolare attenzione a Mario Hermoso e Marten de Roon. Per il difensore spagnolo sarebbe già pronto un nuovo contratto biennale, mentre il centrocampista olandese potrebbe prolungare la propria permanenza nella Capitale per un'ulteriore stagione. Due operazioni che permetterebbero alla società di dare continuità all'organico, confermando elementi considerati importanti per il progetto tecnico. Secondo quanto riferisce Il Messaggero, restano invece in stand-by le trattative per i rinnovi di Paulo Dybala e Lorenzo Pellegrini. La società ha deciso di rimandare ogni valutazione alla fine della stagione, concentrandosi per il momento sugli obiettivi sportivi. Intanto arrivano indicazioni incoraggianti sulle condizioni dell'attaccante argentino, che sarà a disposizione per la trasferta contro il Parma. Dybala, che oggi festeggia il suo trentatreesimo compleanno, sta svolgendo anche allenamenti supplementari per migliorare la condizione fisica. L'obiettivo è farsi trovare pronto per dare il proprio contributo alla squadra, sia nell'eventualità di una maglia da titolare sia entrando a partita in corso.

Il futuro di Kevin De Bruyne al Napoli torna in discussione, con il PSV Eindhoven pronto ad anticipare i tempi per provare a portarlo in Olanda. Il club avrebbe inizialmente programmato un tentativo per la prossima estate, ma starebbe ora valutando la possibilità di intervenire già durante il mercato di gennaio. Secondo quanto riportato da Sky Sport, i primi contatti tra le società sarebbero già avvenuti e nei prossimi giorni potrebbero esserci nuovi sviluppi. L'interesse del PSV si inserisce in una situazione che, nonostante i chiarimenti delle ultime settimane, non avrebbe ancora restituito certezze sulla permanenza del centrocampista belga. Sul rapporto con Massimiliano Allegri avrebbero pesato anche alcuni malintesi, apparentemente superati, ma la prospettiva di un trasferimento resta concreta qualora si presentassero le condizioni giuste. L'ostacolo principale riguarda la formula dell'eventuale operazione. Il Napoli non sarebbe disposto a liberare De Bruyne a parametro zero, dopo aver sostenuto un investimento economico importante per assicurarsi le prestazioni del giocatore. La dirigenza azzurra chiederebbe quindi un indennizzo per autorizzarne la partenza, lasciando al PSV il compito di formulare una proposta adeguata. La trattativa è ancora in una fase iniziale e molto dipenderà dalla volontà del club olandese di anticipare un'operazione originariamente prevista per giugno. Il Napoli non ha dunque chiuso alla possibilità di una cessione, ma non intende rinunciare al belga senza una contropartita economica. I prossimi contatti serviranno a capire se l'interesse del PSV potrà trasformarsi in una vera negoziazione durante la sessione invernale.

Il futuro di Edon Zhegrova alla Juventus potrebbe essere lontano da Torino. L'esterno offensivo kosovaro, finora impiegato prevalentemente come alternativa da Luciano Spalletti, vorrebbe giocare con maggiore continuità e conquistare una maglia da titolare. Un obiettivo complicato dalla concorrenza nel reparto, soprattutto in vista dei rientri di Francisco Conceicao e Kenan Yildiz. Con Alajbegovic, Boga e Nico Gonzalez a completare le opzioni offensive, il classe 1999 sta valutando la possibilità di cambiare squadra già a gennaio.

Come racconta Tuttosport, tra le possibili destinazioni del kosovaro c'è l'Al Ittihad, che aveva già tentato di acquistarlo negli ultimi giorni del mercato estivo. Il grave infortunio del giovane Fernandes, indisponibile fino ad aprile, potrebbe spingere il club saudita a tornare alla carica. Attenzione anche al Monaco, alla ricerca di un esterno offensivo per il 4-2-3-1 di Filipe Luis. Trovano invece pochi riscontri le indiscrezioni sul Besiktas, che dopo l'arrivo di Ernest Poku sembra orientato verso altri ruoli.

La dirigenza bianconera dovrà decidere se continuare a puntare sull'ex Lille oppure sfruttare il suo mercato per ottenere risorse da reinvestire. Una cessione a gennaio, soprattutto in caso di offerta importante dall'Arabia Saudita, permetterebbe alla Juventus di finanziare nuovi acquisti senza appesantire il bilancio. La priorità resta consegnare a Spalletti rinforzi offensivi per la corsa al quarto posto, mentre Zhegrova cerca un progetto che possa garantirgli un ruolo da protagonista.

La Juventus non ha dimenticato Alexander Sorloth. Nonostante gli arrivi estivi di Randal Kolo Muani e Nick Woltemade, il centravanti norvegese dell'Atletico Madrid continua a essere uno degli obiettivi preferiti di Luciano Spalletti. L'allenatore bianconero ne apprezza le caratteristiche, differenti rispetto a quelle degli attaccanti attualmente a disposizione, e lo segue da tempo. Già prima dell'estate la Juventus aveva approfondito il suo profilo, arrivando a valutare un'operazione con gli spagnoli che avrebbe potuto coinvolgere Nico Gonzalez.

Secondo quanto racconta La Gazzetta dello Sport, i contatti tra Juventus e Atletico Madrid potrebbero riprendere sfruttando una nuova pedina: Jonathan David. Il canadese, trasferitosi in Spagna dopo le difficoltà incontrate a Torino, ha realizzato finora tre gol e due assist e potrebbe diventare la chiave dell'operazione. L'ipotesi è quella di uno scambio tra centravanti con valutazioni intorno ai 25-30 milioni di euro. Una soluzione gradita anche all'amministratore delegato Giovanni Carnevali, che riuscirebbe ad accontentare Spalletti e a realizzare una cessione utile per i conti del club, considerando i vincoli del settlement agreement sottoscritto con l'UEFA.

I primi segnali sull'asse Torino-Madrid sarebbero incoraggianti, anche perché Sorloth non ha dimenticato il corteggiamento bianconero. La Juventus, tuttavia, continua a valutare alternative in vista di gennaio. Tra i nomi monitorati figurano Folarin Balogun del Monaco e Gianluca Scamacca dell'Atalanta, già conosciuto da Carnevali ai tempi del Sassuolo. Resta nella lista anche Mateo Retegui, sebbene al momento l'ex attaccante atalantino non sembri particolarmente intenzionato a cambiare squadra.

TER STEGEN SUL FUTURO TRA AJAX E BARCELLONA: “OGGI NON POSSO SAPERLO - ”   Futuro tutto da scrivere quello di Marc-André Ter Stegen. Il portiere tedesco attualmente milita nell'Ajax, club che lo ha prelevato in prestito dal Barcellona e dove sta tenendo un rendimento ottimo. Inevitabile che si pongano le prime domande riguardo alla prossima stagione. Interrogato sulla questione, ai microfoni di Sport Bild, ha dichiarato: "Siamo solo a novembre, quindi non posso davvero dire cosa succederà in estate". Difficile, dunque, al momento capire se tornerà in blaugrana oppure se resterà a difendere la porta dei lancieri (o altre opzioni). L'ipotesi che possa tornare al Barcellona appare la più remota. Il tecnico Flick ha a disposizione due portieri di alto livello come Joan García e Livakovic. In più c'è Szczesny, il cui contratto è in scadenza e non verrà rinnovato. L'intenzione di Ter Stegen è di fare il titolare: motivo in più per allontanare il ritorno in Catalogna.

"Le mancherà Cristiano Ronaldo?", questa una delle domande che sono state poste al commissario tecnico del Portogallo, Jorge Jesus, dopo la sconfitta interna dei suoi contro la Danimarca. È stato il primo impegno dei lusitani dopo l'addio alla nazionale da parte di CR7, e non è finita bene: 1-4 il pesante passivo in casa.

E la risposta di Jorge Jesus? L'allenatore è stato dubbioso e ha fatto notare che quello di Cristiano Ronaldo non sia più un tema d'attualità per il suo lavoro, vista la decisione presa dal giocatore. "Se sento la mancanza di Cristiano Ronaldo? In che modo e per cosa potrebbe mancarmi? Cristiano non è più in nazionale", le sue parole.

E ancora, il tecnico ha aggiunto: "Forse mi manca solamente per farmi compagnia. Lui non gioca più con il Portogallo". "Non è più qui con noi" - ha fatto ancora notare - "ha già deciso lui cosa volesse fare".

#2083. West Ham should be keeping tabs on situation of out-of-favour Leeds United striker: Opinion

West Ham have a chance to propel themselves into title-winning contention in the January transfer window. WHU have been impressive to start the year and are the clear top scorers in the Championship, despite struggling to nail down a number nine.

West Ham United should be looking at Mateo Joseph as a potential January addition, with the Leeds United forward offering an interesting opportunity for Scott Parker as he looks to guide the Hammers back into the Premier League.

Parker has inherited a side with plenty of attacking quality, but the centre-forward position remains an area that could benefit from strengthening. With Joseph looking to be available in January, West Ham must be paying attention to his situation.

Joel Piroe has scored around four league goals since arriving on loan from Leeds, while Taty Castellanos has struggled to establish himself as a consistent goalscoring threat. West Ham are scoring freely, with 37 goals in their opening 15 Championship fixtures, but another option could prove important during the second half of the campaign.

Joseph would offer something different. The 23-year-old spent last season on loan at Mallorca, making 29 La Liga appearances, including 19 starts.

He registered two goals and three assists, with his underlying numbers suggesting there could be more to come from him in front of goal. His 4.92 expected goals compared with two actual strikes indicates that his finishing did not necessarily reflect the opportunities he found, according to FotMob.

Versatility is another attraction. Primarily a centre-forward or right winger, Joseph can operate across the frontline, giving Parker additional tactical flexibility. He also has experience of winning promotion from the Championship, having featured 39 times for Leeds during their successful 2024/25 campaign, recording three goals and three assists.

There is, however, an obvious complication. Joseph suffered an ACL injury while at Mallorca in April and has been recovering at Leeds. He is targeting a return to competitive action around January or February 2027, meaning any potential move would carry considerable fitness risk.

His modest senior goalscoring record also means West Ham would be taking a chance rather than signing an established Championship marksman. Nevertheless, that could make him an attainable target. Leeds are reportedly open to moving him on, while his injury situation could create an opportunity for a loan agreement with a potential obligation to buy.

West Ham need to be careful with their January recruitment, particularly with promotion within reach. However, Joseph’s age, versatility and previous Championship experience make him an intriguing option. If his recovery progresses as hoped, he could provide valuable competition for Piroe without requiring a significant initial investment.

#2081. Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

Jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

Newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

Newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

The North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

Referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059

A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

Elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

Chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

Newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

Newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

Woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

Play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

Time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

Rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

Leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

Bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

Newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

Corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

Newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

Newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

Lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

That was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

Good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

The game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

On the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

Leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a big threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

Leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

Fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

Matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

The former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane

Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa

Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave

Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq

Newcastle United continue their preparations for the new season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

New manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#2079. Moreira discusses starring in the derby, wearing Kaka’s number and De Winter declining call-up

Diego Moreira has admitted the last few weeks have been ‘complicated’ for AC Milan, but he was delighted to star in the derby.

Having arrived in the summer window for a fee reported to be just over €50m, Moreira has hit the ground running at his new club. The brace against Lazio was a big introduction, inspiring a comeback, then his three goal contributions made it four derby wins in a row for the Rossoneri.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There is even talk that the fee paid is beginning to look like a bargain, given that the former Benfica man is capable of playing multiple positions but appears to be decisive no matter what. Now, a key role with the national team will follow.

Moreira gave an interview to RTL Sports from the Belgian national team’s training camp, where he would normally be joined by Alexis Saelemaekers and Koni De Winter. However, the former is injured and the latter turned down the call-up.

How have the past few weeks been for you?

“These were quite complicated weeks, because we played so many games back-to-back. We also had some players injured, so it was a very intense period. But it was up to us to prepare well for the derby.

“We know how important a derby is in Italy. We played the match to our fullest, imposing our pace and our game. I was decisive in that match, but, as I said, it was also thanks to the help of my team-mates. It’s something that will remain forever etched in my memory.”

“It’s an honour to wear his number and to represent such a player. But, as I said, I’m building my career and also trying to establish myself. It’s still an honour to wear that number.”

What do you think of De Winter’s decision to decline a call-up?

“It’s a personal matter, his choice. It’s something between him and the coach. I’m not the one who should discuss it, neither in terms of his life nor his playing time.

“It’s a question you should ask him directly. Van Bommel’s trust is certainly a good thing, but that doesn’t mean I should rest on my laurels.”

#2078. Southampton loanee has chance to kickstart his spell after Keven Schlotterbeck injury: Opinion

Southampton had a mixed summer transfer window but one major blow was the sale of Taylor Harwood-Bellis. The Saints brought in multiple defenders in a bid to replace him and one of which was Zach Abbott who joined on loan.

Abbott has a chance to change the course of his Southampton loan spell following Keven Schlotterbeck’s shoulder injury. The Nottingham Forest youngster was introduced during the 1-0 defeat at Preston North End and delivered a composed performance across 79 minutes at centre-back, earning a 6.8 FotMob rating.

It was only his second Championship appearance since arriving on loan in September, but the circumstances have created an opportunity he desperately needs. At 20, Abbott is still developing, and regular first-team football was the obvious attraction of his temporary move to St Mary’s.

Abbott has been honest about his frustration at the lack of minutes, admitting to BBC Radio Solent that he has been “itching for a lot more”. His response to limited opportunities has been to remain patient, work hard in training and take advice from his experienced teammates.

The numbers underline how little football Abbott has played. He has accumulated just 124 Championship minutes across two appearances, completing 74 of his 84 passes at an impressive 88.1% accuracy. He has also won two of his three aerial duels, with his success rate ranking in the 86th percentile among full-backs.

Although the sample size is small, his Preston performance offered encouragement that he can handle the demands of Championship football. His versatility is another advantage, having previously demonstrated an ability to operate at both centre-back and right-back.

Southampton are 7th after 15 games, with 24 points, and remain firmly in the promotion conversation. However, Schlotterbeck’s expected six-week absence leaves Tonda Eckert needing to find a reliable defensive replacement. Nathan Wood and Jack Stephens provide competition, but Abbott has already shown he can step in without looking out of place.

This is an important period for Abbott and both clubs. He joined Southampton to gain the senior experience that was difficult to secure at Nottingham Forest, but his lack of involvement has reportedly raised the possibility of a January recall.

A sustained run of appearances before the new year would change that picture considerably. It would provide Forest with the Championship experience they wanted him to gain and give Southampton another capable defensive option during a crucial period of their campaign.

The upcoming home fixture against Derby County after the international break could be particularly important. Abbott has already reached an FA Cup semi-final and featured in the Europa League, so his potential is clear.

Now he needs regular opportunities to demonstrate it at Championship level. Schlotterbeck’s injury is unfortunate, but it could be the opening Abbott has been waiting for. Southampton should give him the chance to make the most of it.

#2077. Marcelo Brozovic, la voglia di tornare in Italia non è nulla rispetto a 10 milioni annui

"L'Al-Sadd annuncia ufficialmente l'ingaggio del giocatore croato Marcelo Brozovic fino al 2027 per unirsi alla prima squadra". Così terminava una delle telenovele dell'estate, almeno una degli ultimi giorni. Perché il croato si era svincolato dall'Al Nassr, dove guadagnava circa 30 milioni di euro all'anno, cercando di ritornare in Italia. Non c'è riuscito soprattutto per le richieste che aveva fatto a tutti i club interessati, dalla Juventus alla Fiorentina: 6 milioni di euro a stagione.

Il club ad avere mosso concretamente verso il croato è stato quello viola, con una proposta biennale da 2,5 milioni di euro. Dopo essere stato cercato dal Real Madrid - con ingaggio anche inferiore - e avere rifiutato Trabzonspor e Monaco, Brozovic avrebbe preferito un rientro in Serie A. Così c'è stata anche una controproposta da parte dell'entourage, non è dato sapere di quanto. Lì si sono chiuse le trattative, anche perché c'erano altre offerte dall'Arabia Saudita e dal Qatar.

Pecunia non olet, verrebbe da dire. Perché poi l'ex interista ha deciso di firmare con l'Al Sadd, club qatariota che lo paga dieci milioni di euro a stagione. Non ha nemmeno tutti i torti, preferendo un campionato meno competitivo e, soprattutto, un cospicuo conto in banca. Oggi Marcelo Brozovic compie 34 anni.

Mauro Baldissoni – the CEO of Monza – made this clear when he spoke to Sky from the Social Football Summit in Turin, explaining the position of the club.

“It’s too easy to talk about just one player and too easy to take credit. We did well, but above all, he did well: he was called upon to make a leap, to make an effort, and he did it very well,” he said.

“Now he’s calm and serene, but he knows he hasn’t achieved anything yet. The foundations are there for a great career. The goal is to have him with us until the end of the season. We know he’s being followed by clubs with great ambitions, but we want to keep him as long as possible.

“It’s still mid-November and no real discussions have been had with anyone. We know that the boy has received some interest through his agent and we’ve received some as well. But it’s all very premature.”

Interest has been confirmed, but from whom? Over the past few weeks, the Portuguese has been closely monitored by scouts from various clubs and strongly linked with several Italian big clubs.

Juventus are looking for another centre-forward to give to Spalletti. Milan want a quality alternative to Gonçalo Ramos and are in the hunt, even if Nicolo Tresoldi has been linked. Inter president Beppe Marotta denied the possibility of adding a fifth striker to the squad, but they are always lurking.

Napoli are closely monitoring the situation too. Massimiliano Allegri has outlined his needs for a striker in the summer to replace Lorenzo Lucca (who is set to leave again), so they are among the frontrunners.

Last summer, Monza paid just €2m to acquire him from Benfica and sign him to a contract until 2030. In just two months, his price has skyrocketed and the asking price is now around €25-30m. Selling in January remains unlikely, unless a big offer is forthcoming.

However, there is the Benfica factor. The Portuguese giants have two clauses in their favour: they will get a 20% share of the capital gain on the player’s future resale, and they have the ability to match any offers that may come from other teams.

#2075. Former Stoke City and Swansea City midfielder completes move to National League promotion hopefuls

Worthing currently sit 6th in the National League table and are eyeing up promotion to the Football League for the first time in their history. Now, they have strengthened their midfield by signing former Stoke City and Swansea City star Sam Clucas, who brings a huge amount of experience to the team.

The 36-year-old was last contracted to Shrewsbury Town, where he played 34 league fixtures last season, scoring two goals and assisting five. He was an important player in the Shrews’ squad last campaign, but his services were not extended further following the summer.

Across his career, Clucas has played in the Premier League, Championship, League One and League Two, and has featured for a multitude of clubs. Hereford, Mansfield Town, Chesterfield, Hull City, Swansea City, Stoke City, Rotherham United, Oldham Athletic, Lincoln City, Shrewsbury Town and now Worthing are the clubs Clucas has represented.

The experienced EFL star will now prepare for life in the fifth tier, with the hope of bringing an historic promotion to the Reds. Worthing are currently in the play-offs, having lost just one league match in their last 11.

Clucas’ experience will be worth its weight in gold, and he has a clear hunger to deliver success to Worthing. “I can see the vision of the club, and I want to be a part of it,” he said in the club statement confirming his arrival.

The former Premier League footballer has plied his trade in the most competitive division in the world and will bring a calm and level head to the National League side, especially as the pressure ramps up later on in the season.

The ex-Stoke City and Swansea City man has already made his debut too. He came on off the bench on Saturday as the Rebels drew 1-1 with Scunthorpe United.

Clucas has penned a one-year deal with the non-league side, but could be offered longer terms if he impresses at the club. If the move proves to be a success, then Worthing will try to tie him down for longer and prolong his playing career.

But if the former Stoke City and Swansea City man fails to hit the heights expected of him, the Reds will not be hurt by his departure next summer, given his contract length.

He has shown he can still play plenty of games after featuring 40 times across the 2025/26 campaign for Shrewsbury Town. Clucas appears to have plenty left in the tank, and he will help to bring squad depth to Worthing as the busiest time of the footballing calendar nears.
